evidence: The probe reads the discovered panel target's committed frame URL and navigation error shape, then evaluates document URL/readiness, runtime identity, and safe SIDE_PANEL context counts in that renderer.
It runs only after the original exact-context guard fails and between the initial and existing follow-up worker reads; the original failure remains fatal even if a later read sees an exact context.

The resulting observations distinguish an uncommitted/unavailable document, failed or wrong navigation, and a committed exact renderer whose runtime context URL remains empty, while correctly treating sequential reads as non-atomic.
A_diagnostic_adequacy.native_cause: unverified; the probe has not run on the pinned hosted Chromium binary, and its diagnostic can itself advance lifecycle.

evidence: Source inspection confirms at most four additional CDP commands on the successful diagnostic path: attach, Page.getFrameTree, Runtime.evaluate, and detach. Each uses the existing CDP send path; no new wait, loop, retry, or timeout was added.
Failure cleanup detaches after attachment; the attach failure path has no session to detach. Probe errors return fixed stage labels without exposing exception text.
Output contains only booleans, readiness state, and counts; raw URLs, target/session/context identifiers, page content, and authentication data are not returned.

The exact imported diagnostic and generated Runtime.evaluate expression passed focused scenarios for loading/unavailable, complete renderer with empty runtime context URL, and interactive renderer with exact runtime context. Assertions covered four-command ordering, privacy, sample ordering, and continued rejection by the original exact-context guard.
